definitions.explanation: A hand tool used to smooth and flatten wood surfaces by shaving thin layers. The traditional Japanese plane ({和|わ}かんな) is pulled toward the user, unlike Western planes which are pushed.

examples.japanese: かんなで{板|いた}の{表面|ひょうめん}を{滑|なめ}らかにする。
examples.english: I smooth the board's surface with a plane.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}がかんなを{引|ひ}くと{薄|うす}い{削|けず}り{屑|くず}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: When the craftsman pulls the plane, thin shavings come off.

examples.japanese: かんなの{刃|は}を{調整|ちょうせい}するのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Adjusting the plane blade is difficult.

notes:
KANJI WRITING:
・{鉋|かんな} (complex kanji, rarely used)
・Usually written in hiragana

JAPANESE vs WESTERN PLANES:
・{和|わ}かんな (Japanese plane) - pulled toward user
・{洋|よう}かんな (Western plane) - pushed away from user
・Japanese style produces finer, thinner shavings

TYPES:
・{平|ひら}かんな (smoothing plane)
・{台直|だいなお}しかんな (jointer plane)
・{面取|めんと}りかんな (chamfer plane)
・{溝|みぞ}かんな (groove plane)

RELATED TERMS:
・かんな{屑|くず}/{削|けず}り{屑|くず} (wood shavings)
・かんな{台|だい} (plane body)
・かんな{刃|ば} (plane blade)

COLLOCATIONS:
・かんなをかける (to plane)
・かんなを{引|ひ}く (to draw a plane)
・かんなで{削|けず}る (to shave with a plane)
・かんなを{研|と}ぐ (to sharpen a plane blade)
